questions.question: Democracy comes from Greek words meaning 'the people' and ____.
The Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution was chaired by Dr ____.
The three levels of Indian government are Union, State and ____.
Mahatma Gandhi's principle of village self-rule is called ____ Swaraj.
The voting age in India is ____ years.
Define 'governance' and list three things that make governance GOOD.
questions.answer: Governance is the way a community organises itself to take decisions and get things done. Good governance has (i) clear RULES, (ii) fair PROCESSES, and (iii) ACCOUNTABILITY — leaders can be questioned if things go wrong.

questions.question: List four features of a democracy.
questions.answer: (i) People CHOOSE their rulers in fair elections. (ii) Every adult has ONE vote of equal value. (iii) Different parties and candidates can compete. (iv) The ruler's power is LIMITED by laws and a Constitution. (v) Citizens have RIGHTS the ruler cannot take away. Any four.

questions.question: What do the words SOVEREIGN, SECULAR and REPUBLIC in our Preamble mean?
questions.answer: SOVEREIGN — independent; no foreign country tells India what to do. SECULAR — the state has no official religion; all religions are treated equally. REPUBLIC — the head of state (the President) is elected, not a hereditary king.

questions.question: Match each subject to the level of government most responsible: (a) defence, (b) state police, (c) village street lights, (d) currency.
questions.answer: (a) defence — Union. (b) state police — State. (c) village street lights — Local. (d) currency — Union.

questions.question: What did the 73rd and 74th Amendments do for local government?
questions.answer: They were passed in 1992. They (i) gave Panchayats (rural) and Municipalities (urban) a constitutional foundation, (ii) required regular elections at the local level, (iii) reserved seats for women and for Scheduled Castes / Scheduled Tribes, and (iv) gave local bodies a clear list of powers and resources.

questions.question: Name three ways an ordinary citizen can participate in democracy beyond voting.
questions.answer: Any three of: contact representatives (write or attend public meetings), stand for election (Panchayat / Municipality / Assembly), form associations and peacefully campaign for causes, use the Right to Information (RTI) to ask government for facts, attend gram-sabha / ward meetings.

questions.question: Why is it not enough for a country to hold elections every five years?
questions.answer: Elections give the people a say once every five years, but in between, a government can act badly. Good governance also needs (i) a FREE PRESS that can criticise the government without fear, (ii) an INDEPENDENT JUDICIARY that can strike down bad laws, (iii) STRONG INSTITUTIONS like the Election Commission and Comptroller-General, and (iv) ACTIVE CIVIL SOCIETY (NGOs, citizens' groups, gram sabhas) to hold the government accountable between elections.

questions.question: Compare a kingdom with a democracy on the three big questions: WHO rules, HOW decisions are made, and HOW power is limited.
questions.answer: WHO rules: in a kingdom, ONE person (the king) rules, usually by birth; in a democracy, the PEOPLE rule, through elected representatives. HOW decisions are made: in a kingdom, by orders from the king and his close advisers; in a democracy, by discussion in assemblies, voting and by laws made through Parliament. HOW power is limited: in a kingdom, the king's power is often UNLIMITED — he can change the law at will; in a democracy, the ruler's power is limited by a written Constitution, by independent courts, by elections, and by citizens' rights that even the ruler cannot take away.

questions.question: A village's well has been broken for two months. The State Capital is 200 km away and the Union Capital is 1,000 km away. Why is the LOCAL government the best level to fix this problem? Use the ideas of Gram Swaraj and the 73rd Amendment in your answer.
questions.answer: The Union and State governments are far away — they cannot easily know the well in this particular village is broken, or which families it serves. The LOCAL Panchayat is closest to the people: it lives with the problem, can inspect it the same day, and can call the gram sabha to take a quick decision. Gandhi's idea of GRAM SWARAJ — village self-rule — argues that strong villages make a strong India, with each village solving its own problems. The 73rd Amendment (1992) gave Panchayats a constitutional foundation, regular elections, reserved seats and clear powers, including over local water, sanitation and basic infrastructure. So fixing the well is exactly the kind of task local government was designed for, and it is faster and more accountable than waiting for instructions from the State or Union capital.
